key_insight: Research agents propose worthwhile experiments, but evidence that their rankings improve which experiment to run remains limited.
engineering_relevance: Use research agents to generate candidate experiments, but validate their prioritization before allocating compute or adopting costlier agent teams.
method: Six frontier models, working alone or in teams, proposed, ranked and forecast minimum viable experiments for seven recent NLP papers.
A separate executor attempted every proposed experiment, including those ranked last.
Three model auditors assessed outcomes; rankings and forecasts were compared with simple baselines.
evidence_signal: Of 415 experiments, 194 were judged sound, valuable and new, and 73 also beyond the seed paper and non-obvious; top-ranked choices beat random selection but were not shown to beat choosing the first-written experiment.
watch_item: Quality judgments relied on model auditors, and teams cost more without a clear overall improvement in proposal quality.
paper_title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment
